title: Triggers and waiting

story: Monday, 09:25. Nova posts its plan for RH-1234 in the ticket's Slack thread, with Approve, Change and Stop buttons. Every minute the Jira poll finds the ticket again, because it is still assigned to Nova, and every time it joins the run that is already waiting. Sean does not click. His phone is off: he is on holiday until next Monday.

What should Nova do? If it waits forever, the ticket looks taken: Nova is the assignee, the board says Awaiting approval, and nobody else picks it up. If it simply ends the run, the poll finds RH-1234 again a minute later, still assigned to Nova, and starts a brand-new run that claims a VM, plans again, and waits again for a man on a beach.
hook.question: How does a run wait for a busy person without waiting forever, and how does it end so that the poll does not start the same work again?

read.h: Assigned to Nova means: Nova's turn
p: Two pieces of the platform meet in one Jira field. The first piece is the trigger. Every Jira trigger in the platform is an entry in one registry, a Map of named queries in the orchestrator. Each entry has a JQL query (Jira's query language), how often to ask, and a function toStart that turns one matching ticket into a workflow and its input. When the orchestrator's worker starts, it turns every entry into a Temporal schedule called poll-jira-<name>, and each tick of the schedule runs the query and calls startRun for every match. Nova's entry asks for tickets assigned to Nova that are not done.

The second piece is the run, which waits for people. And the field they share is the assignee. As long as RH-1234 is assigned to Nova, the poll keeps calling startRun for it. While the run is open, that is harmless, because the second start joins the open run, as you saw in the lesson about one run per ticket. But the moment the run finishes, its name is free again, and the next tick starts a fresh run. So the assignee works like a switch: assigned to Nova means "Nova, this is your turn", and every way a run ends must flip the switch back to a person.

notes.text: The poll runs as the Nova service account, so currentUser() means Nova. This line is the switch: change the assignee and the ticket leaves the query.
The requester is read from Jira's changelog: the last person who set the assignee to Nova.
The same ticket every minute is fine while the run is open. Once it has finished, the same call starts a new run.

deeper.h: Go deeper: one registry, schedules made at start-up
p: The registry exists so that every agent starts work the same safe way. Nova registers "nova", the bug fixers register their own queries every 5 minutes, and none of them writes schedule code. ensureSchedules runs every time the orchestrator's worker starts: it creates each schedule, or, when create throws ScheduleAlreadyRunning, updates the one that exists, so a deploy never makes a second schedule. Each schedule uses the overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window as long as its interval, the two rules from the lesson about schedules, so a slow Jira or an outage never produces a pile of polls.

Every start goes through startRun, so the walls from earlier lessons hold for every trigger: one run per thing, and the kill switch, which makes startRun refuse new runs of a stopped agent. If Jira is down, the activity fails and its retry policy tries again later; nothing else breaks.

A run waits for a person in three places: a plan that needs a decision, a question that needs an answer, and a PR that needs a review. Each wait has two times, counted from the start of the wait: when to remind, and when to give up. A plan is reminded after 1 day and handed back after 3. A question is reminded after 1 day and handed back after 2, because Nova is in the middle of the work. A review is reminded after 2 days and the PR is closed with a note after 14, because reviewers plan their week.

All three go through one function, waitForPerson, so they behave the same way. It is two calls to condition() with a timeout, which you know from the lesson about signals and timers: each call resolves true as soon as its function returns true, or false when the time runs out, and the waiting itself is a durable timer that costs nothing. The important detail is what the function checks. It is not only "did the person act?" but "did the person act, or did someone press Stop?", so a Stop ends any wait at once, without a reminder.

Nova reminds exactly once. A reminder costs the person's attention, and a bot that pings every few hours teaches people to mute its thread, which is worse than no reminder at all. One reminder, and then a clear hand-back, is what a polite colleague does.

notes.text: On a drill ticket, scaled turns days into minutes, so a test can walk the whole path in one sitting.
Stop is part of every wait. It wins over both timers.

One reminder in the Slack thread that mentions the requester. peopleApis is the activity proxy for Jira and Slack calls, which keeps retrying through an outage, and notify falls back to a Jira comment when Slack is down.
The wait ran out: give the ticket back (next section). For a review, this step closes the PR with a note instead.

deeper.h: Go deeper: false means two things
p: waitForPerson returns false both when the ticket was handed back and when a person pressed Stop, because in both cases the run must not continue. The caller must not guess which one happened. It reads the run's state and picks the right ending, so a ticket that Sean stopped is reported as Stopped, not as Parked:
if (!(await waitForPerson(run, "plan", () => decision !== undefined, t))) return run.stopped ? "stopped" : "parked";

read.h: Every ending gives the ticket back
p: Handing back, which the platform also calls parking a ticket, does two things: it posts why, in the thread and on the ticket, and it makes the requester the assignee again. Do not confuse it with parking a VM. Parking a VM stops the machine and keeps its disk while the run goes on waiting, for example 10 minutes after Nova asked a question. Parking a ticket ends the run.

The assignment back is the part that matters most, for two reasons. First, a ticket must always have a person as its owner, so that Sean sees RH-1234 on his own board when he returns. Second, it is the switch from the first section. If the hand-back only posted a note and left Nova as the assignee, the poll would start a fresh run a minute later. That run would claim a VM, write the same plan again, wait three more days, remind Sean again, and so on for as long as he is away. In the lab you will break the hand-back on purpose and watch exactly this loop.

The same rule covers the two other endings. Stop, from the Slack button, /nova stop or @Nova stop on the ticket, saves a checkpoint if a VM is running, releases the VM, keeps the branch and the notes, and assigns the ticket back. And when Nova marks its PR ready, the ticket goes back to the requester too, because from then on a person is in charge. When Sean comes back and assigns RH-1234 to Nova again, the poll matches it, startRun finds no open run, and a fresh run nova:RH-1234 begins, with the branch nova/RH-1234 and the notes still there.
read.see:
10:06:42  RH-1234  posted the plan in Slack and Jira, released i-0001
10:06:52  RH-1234  Slack thread: "@sean, the plan is still waiting for your decision."
10:07:12  RH-1234  "Nobody decided on the plan in 3 days, so I am handing the ticket back."  assignee: sean
(from the lab: a drill ticket, where one day lasts 10 seconds)

deeper.h: Go deeper: unassigning Nova is a Stop, but Nova's own hand-back is not
p: There is a fourth way to press Stop: a person changes the assignee away from Nova. The poll notices the change in the ticket's history and sends the stop signal to the open run. The trap is that the hand-back also changes the assignee away from Nova. So the rule looks at who made the change: a change by anyone except Nova is a Stop, and Nova's own change is just the run ending as planned.

lab.title: Remind once, then give it back
needs: The course repo at ~/Projects/ai-agents-course (the lab starts from the p7-4 lab's files)
lab.goal: Run a Jira poll as a real Temporal schedule against a pretend Jira, make a waiting run remind once and hand the ticket back, and see that a ticket handed back stays out of the poll until a person assigns it again.

guess.q: Nova's plan for RH-1234 has waited 3 days. The run posts a note and ends, but leaves Nova as the assignee. The poll asks Jira every minute. What happens next?

options.text: Nothing: the run is finished, so the ticket is done for Nova
options.why: The poll does not know the run's story. It only sees a ticket assigned to Nova, and a finished run frees its name for a new run.

options.text: Within a minute the poll starts a fresh run nova:RH-1234, which plans again on a new VM and waits again
options.why: Assigned to Nova means "start or join". With no open run to join, startRun starts a new one, and the loop repeats every three days.

options.text: The poll joins the finished run and gets its result
options.why: USE_EXISTING only joins runs that are still open. A finished run cannot be joined.

lab.build: Write waitForPerson in workflows.mjs, following the comment above it: wait with condition() until done() is true or a Stop arrived (run.stoppedBy is set), up to the reminder time; if nothing happened, send one reminder with people.notify; wait again for the rest of the time; if still nothing, call people.handBack with the park note and return false. Return !run.stoppedBy when a wait ends early. Restart the worker (Ctrl+C, node worker.mjs) and run node clean.mjs: the poll starts a fresh run within 5 seconds. Watch the reminder at 10 seconds and the hand-back at 30. Then play Sean coming back: node assign.mjs RH-1234 Nova, and once the plan is posted, temporal workflow signal --workflow-id nova:RH-1234 --name decidePlan --input '"approve"'. Finally assign it again and press Stop instead: temporal workflow signal --workflow-id nova:RH-1234 --name stop --input '"sean"'.
checks: The worker terminal shows exactly one reminder about 10 seconds after the plan was posted, and the hand-back about 20 seconds after that, ending with assignee: sean.
temporal workflow result --workflow-id nova:RH-1234 shows Result "Parked".
Ten seconds later, temporal workflow count --query "WorkflowType='ticketToPr' AND ExecutionStatus='Running'" says Total: 0, although the poll is still running every 5 seconds.
After node assign.mjs RH-1234 Nova, a new run with the same ID plans within 5 seconds, and the approve signal ends it with "PR open: draft PR #2512".
A stop signal during the wait ends the run at once with "Stopped by sean", with no reminder line, and the ticket is assigned to sean.
lab.fix: A teammate says "assigning tickets is Jira's job, not ours" and deletes the line in handBack that sets the assignee, keeping only the note. Make the same change, restart the worker, run node assign.mjs RH-1234 Nova and wait two minutes. The hand-back line now ends with assignee: Nova, and right after it the worker claims a new lite VM and writes the same plan again; temporal workflow list shows a new finished run nova:RH-1234 every 35 seconds, and Sean gets the same reminder each time. Put the line back.
explain: Why must every way a run ends, including Stop and a ready PR, make the requester the assignee again?
Why is the Stop check inside both condition() calls, and what would happen if it were only checked after the waits?
Why does Nova remind once and then hand back, instead of reminding every day until the person answers?
lab.done: A plan that nobody decides is reminded once and handed back, the poll leaves a handed-back ticket alone until it is assigned again, and you stopped the worker and the dev server with Ctrl+C.

check.q: Why does every way a run ends assign the ticket back to the requester?

options.text: Because Jira refuses to close a ticket that has no assignee
options.why: The run does not close the ticket, and Jira allows tickets without an assignee. The reason is the poll and the owner.

options.text: Because the poll starts or joins a run for every ticket assigned to Nova, and a ticket must always have a person as its owner
options.why: Leaving Nova as the assignee would start a fresh run a minute later and hide the ticket from the person who has to act.

options.text: So that the next poll can join the finished run and read its result
options.why: Finished runs cannot be joined. The point is the opposite: the poll should not touch the ticket at all.

check.q: Sean presses Stop on day 2 of a plan wait. What does waitForPerson do?

options.text: It waits until day 3 and then hands the ticket back
options.why: Stop is part of the condition, so the wait ends the moment the stop signal arrives.

options.text: It sends the day-1 reminder again, then ends
options.why: The reminder was already sent on day 1, and a Stop never sends one.

options.text: It returns false at once, and the caller sees that the run was stopped and reports Stopped
options.why: false only says "do not continue"; the run's state says why, so a stopped ticket is not reported as parked.

check.q: Why does Nova send one reminder, and not one every day until somebody answers?

options.text: Repeated reminders cost people's attention and teach them to mute the thread; after the hand-back the ticket is on the person's board anyway
options.why: One reminder and then a clear hand-back keeps Nova's messages worth reading.

options.text: Temporal allows only two timers in one workflow
options.why: A workflow can have many timers. The limit is a choice about people, not about Temporal.

options.text: Slack would block the app for posting too often
options.why: One message a day is far below any Slack limit. The reason is people, not rate limits.

p: The registry and the schedules live in ai-agents/orchestrator/src/triggers/schedules.ts: QUERIES, startMatches and ensureSchedules, which the orchestrator's worker runs at start-up; the polls run as pollJira on the ai-agents-orchestrator queue. Nova's entry is triggers/nova.ts (every minute, assignee = currentUser() as the Nova service account), and the bug fixers add theirs. The Jira token comes from Vault at infrastructure/ai-agents/jira-nova and reaches the orchestrator workers only.

waitForPerson lives in orchestrator/src/waiting.ts and is used by ticketToPr for the plan, the questions and the review. G3-38 calls the last step parkTicket; G4-05 adds the assign-back for Stop, for a hand-back and for a PR marked ready, and treats an assignee change away from Nova by anyone but Nova as Stop. Two details to fix while you build: the G3-38 helper returns false for a Stop too, so ticketToPr must read run.stopped before it reports "parked", and the reminder and the hand-back should use peopleApis, the retry policy for Jira and Slack calls, so a long outage of both never makes them give up.

tickets.why: The registry of Jira queries, startMatches, pollJira and ensureSchedules.
waitForPerson: the three waits, one reminder, the hand-back, Stop, drill mode.
Nova's registry entry: the JQL, the requester from the changelog.
Assign back on Stop, hand-back and ready; unassigning Nova is a Stop, Nova's own change is not.

words.plain: One Map of named Jira queries; each becomes a schedule poll-jira-<name> that starts or joins runs through startRun.
The one helper for every wait on a person: wait, remind once, wait, hand back; Stop ends it at once.
Say why and make the requester the assignee again; the run ends. Not the same as parking a VM.
A test ticket where the same waits last minutes instead of days.
The person who assigned the ticket to Nova, read from Jira's history. Reminders mention them, and the ticket goes back to them.

review.q: From memory: the remind and hand-back times of the three waits.
review.a: Plan 1 day and 3 days, question 1 day and 2 days, review 2 days and 14 days (the PR is closed with a note).

review.q: A teammate wants the hand-back to keep Nova as the assignee "so Nova can continue later". What happens, and what do you suggest?
review.a: The poll starts a fresh run a minute later and repeats the plan and the wait forever. Hand the ticket back; to continue later, a person assigns it to Nova again, and the branch and notes are still there.

review.q: Why is a Stop checked inside the waits and not only after them?
review.a: condition() wakes up whenever the run's state changes, so a Stop inside the check ends the wait the moment it arrives, without a reminder or days of waiting.

remember: Remind once, then give the ticket back to a person, because as long as Nova is the assignee the poll will start the work again.
